Accepted grammar (scheme case-insensitive, ASCII host incl. bracketed IPv6 without zone, port 1..65535, optional base path) with everything else IAE; base path passes the §3.2 segment and character checks; null -> NPE.

Host first, client headers in received order minus removed with merged Cookie at first Cookie position, then X-Forwarded-For/Proto/Host, then .requestHeader values in option order, then framing header and Connection: close.

Comma split + OWS trim, Content-Length elements digits fitting a long compared numerically; Transfer-Encoding lines comma-joined, empty elements ignored, case-insensitive names, parameterised coding or empty value treated as non-chunked under both framing tables.
Framing headers validated on every response before skipping HEAD/204/304 bodies; valid length or -1 passed to relay for HEAD/304, -1 for 204.

extra_findings.description: D-055 says the proxy sends no X-Forwarded-For when 'no usable socket address exists' but never defines 'usable'. Request.socketAddress() returns a non-null String as the adapter reports it (Request.java:132-141), so an empty value, a host name (servlet container with lookups on) or a malformed literal could either be appended to X-Forwarded-For or dropped. That is observable at the backend, and AMB-26 asked about 'not an IP literal' specifically.
extra_findings.suggested_item: A socket address is usable for X-Forwarded-For only when, after removing surrounding brackets and any '%zone', it parses as an IPv4 or IPv6 literal (the parse ProxyTrustSetting.Cidr.address already performs); otherwise the client X-Forwarded-For is dropped and none is sent.
